# fingerprintd usage guide for AI agents

`fingerprintd` is a server-authoritative device-fingerprinting service for
anti-fraud and anti-automation. The client only collects evidence; the server
issues a one-time challenge, fuzzy-matches the evidence against its fingerprint
library, fuses passive network signals, and returns `visitorId` + `confidence` +
`decision`. The identity is never computed on the client, so it cannot be forged
or replayed.

Primary docs:

- README: https://github.com/WuChenDi/fingerprintd/blob/main/README.md
- Design spec: https://github.com/WuChenDi/fingerprintd/blob/main/DESIGN.md
- Repository: https://github.com/WuChenDi/fingerprintd

## What it is

- One compute engine (`crates/fp-core`, published as `fingerprintd-core`), two deployment targets: a native Axum
  server (`crates/fingerprintd`) and a Cloudflare Worker (`apps/edge`, running
  `fp-core` compiled to WASM). A client works against either unchanged.
- A browser SDK (`@cdlab/fingerprintd`) wraps FingerprintJS/BotD, computes
  the nonce freshness probe in WASM, and submits — it never derives an id.
- A browser playground (`apps/web`) drives the full flow and visualizes what the
  client sends vs. what the server judges.
- A config-gated risk route on the edge Worker (`apps/edge`, `POST /checkin/assess`)
  consumes `/identify` output plus its own account/device/IP/time aggregation to
  score check-in anti-farming — the reference example of turning fingerprintd
  signals into an allow/challenge/deny decision without modifying the core; the
  playground (`apps/web`) demos it.

## The flow

1. `GET /challenge` — the server mints a one-time nonce (short TTL, single-use)
   and returns it plus the collection plan.
2. The client collects `stable_components` (canvas / webgl / fonts / audio /
   screen / UA …, with NO nonce mixed in — this is the identity-matching input),
   and optionally a `probe = hex(HMAC-SHA256(key, nonce))` computed in WASM (a
   freshness proof, never a matching signal).
3. `POST /identify { nonce, stable_components, probe?, ts? }` — the server burns
   the nonce (replay protection), recalls candidates by blocking keys, scores them
   with the Fellegi–Sunter model, fuses passive JA4/IP signals, and returns the
   identity.

## Endpoints

Both stacks serve the same wire contract:

- `GET /health` — liveness (`200 OK`).
- `GET /challenge` — issue a one-time nonce challenge.
- `POST /identify` — compute `visitorId` + `confidence` + `decision`. The request
  body is `deny_unknown_fields`: an unexpected top-level key is rejected `400`. A
  reused/expired nonce, or a failed enforced probe/timestamp check, returns `401`.
- `DELETE /visitor/{id}` — GDPR erasure. Gated by `admin_key` (route disabled when
  unset); idempotent (`204` even if the visitor did not exist).

`/identify` returns:

```json
{
  "visitorId": "string",
  "confidence": 0.0,
  "decision": "match | review | new_device",
  "is_new_device": false,
  "collision_risk": false,
  "signals": { "ua_tls_consistent": true, "ip_risk": "low | medium | high" }
}
```

`confidence` is DECISION confidence, not identity trust: a brand-new device
resolves as `new_device` with high confidence. Read `is_new_device` / `decision`
for identity trust, not `confidence` alone.

## Run the native server

```bash
cargo run -p fingerprintd                                   # 127.0.0.1:8080
FINGERPRINTD_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:9000 cargo run -p fingerprintd
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
```

Log level is `RUST_LOG` (default `info`).

## Call it from a browser

```ts
import { createCollector, run } from '@cdlab/fingerprintd'

const { identity } = await run({
  baseUrl: 'https://fp.example.com',
  collect: createCollector(),   // FingerprintJS + BotD + WASM probe
})
```

## Configuration

Layered, increasing priority: built-in defaults → `fingerprintd.toml` →
`FINGERPRINTD_`-prefixed environment variables. Native-server keys:

- `FINGERPRINTD_BIND_ADDR` (default `127.0.0.1:8080`) — listen address.
- `FINGERPRINTD_NONCE_TTL_SECS` (default `30`) — one-time nonce lifetime.
- `FINGERPRINTD_PROBE_KEY` (unset) — HMAC key enabling nonce-probe verification.
- `FINGERPRINTD_RESPONSE_SIGNING_KEY` (unset) — HMAC key enabling `/identify`
  response signatures (`x-fp-timestamp` + `x-fp-signature`).
- `FINGERPRINTD_ENFORCE_TS_WINDOW` (default `false`) + `FINGERPRINTD_TS_SKEW_SECS`
  (default `30`) — request timestamp window.
- `FINGERPRINTD_ADMIN_KEY` (unset) — Bearer key gating `DELETE /visitor/{id}`.
- `FINGERPRINTD_RETENTION_SECS` (default `0`, disabled) — evict records past this age.
- `FINGERPRINTD_FUZZY_MAX_RECORDS` (default `1000000`) — max distinct visitors.
- `FINGERPRINTD_FUZZY_RECORD_TTL_SECS` (default `0`, disabled) — evict unseen records.
- `FINGERPRINTD_FUZZY_MAX_BLOCK` (default `1024`) — per-block visitor cap.
- `FINGERPRINTD_FUZZY_MAX_FREQUENCY_VALUES` (default `1000000`) — tracked `u_i` value cap.

The `probe_key` / `response_signing_key` / `admin_key` controls are fail-closed and
off by default — each activates only once its key is set. The capacity bounds apply
to the native server only; the stateless edge is per-request. The native store is
process-local (a restart re-mints devices); use the edge (Durable Object + D1) or an
external store behind the `NonceStore` / `FingerprintStore` / `CandidateSource`
traits for a persistent, stable `visitorId`.

## Trust boundaries (do not misreport as vulnerabilities)

- Passive signals (JA4/IP) are read server-side from the connection, never from the
  client body, and only when the deployment trusts the edge (`trust_edge_headers`).
- The probe and response-signing keys embedded in client WASM/JS are defense in
  depth, not decisive; extracting them is expected. The one-time nonce and TLS are
  the primary guarantees. An L3 adversary forging a single signal is a documented
  limitation.

## Design

`DESIGN.md` is the authoritative spec: architecture (§1–§9) and fuzzy-matching
engine (§1–§12). Source doc-comments reference its sections as `architecture §N` /
`fuzzy-matching §N`. Read it before proposing changes to the matching model, the
challenge-response split, the passive-signal trust boundary, or the HTTP contract.
